edits.text: Do not cut immediately after a finite auxiliary or copula (e.g. when the marker follows a clause head like a finite 'be' or auxiliary); such cuts split the verb from its complement and often produce contradiction or lost cohesion.
When two candidates lie inside the same noun phrase, prefer the later candidate that leaves the entire NP intact (choose the marker immediately after the NP over one inside it).
edits._was: - When one cut yields a full independent clause after the marker and another cuts earlier inside a long noun phrase, prefer the later cut that delivers a full clause to the listener.
